To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the relativistic baryonic chiral perturbation calculation at order $q^{4}$ does not generate sufficient curvatures in the Sachs form factors, and (ii) the electric form factor is very sensitive to the higher-order contributions.

the electric and magnetic form factors are not sufficiently well described by a one-loop calculation and that the electric neutron form factor is very sensitive to the inclusion of higher-order corrections.

the one-loop results for the electromagnetic form factors in baryon chimal perturbation theory are in good agreement with experimental data for the proton, but not for the neutron; and that the one-loop result for the magnetic form factor of the proton is too flat, while the electric form factor is too steep.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
relativistic chiral perturbation is a promising tool for the description of the nucleon electromagnetic form factors, but that the present one-loop calculations are still insufficient.

a relativistic one-loop calculation of $F_1$, $F_2$ and the electric Sachs form factor of the proton is in very good agreement with the data, whereas the neutron's electric form factor is in need of higher-order corrections.
the relativistic formulation is the most consistent one, and it should be the basis for future calculations of higher-order contributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relativistic approach to baryon chidal perturbation theory is the appropriate one for calculating nucleon form factors.
the relativistic approach provides a consistent framework to calculate the electromagnetic form factors of baryons.
the relativistic baryonic formulation of chiral perturbation is a very powerful framework to study the nucleon electromagnetic form factors.
